attempts.label: DANDI:000959
attempts.paper_title: Closed-loop microstimulations of the orbitofrontal cortex during real-life gaze interaction enhance dynamic social attention
attempts.entry_title: Closed-loop OFC microstimulation and dynamic social attention (Fan et al. 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Fan, Dal Monte, Nair, Fagan and Chang (2024) on dandiset 000959, which holds the gaze, pupil, fixation events and stimulation times of every run of the 81 Eyes and 15 Mouth stimulation days of two stimulated monkeys. It compares social gaze distance, its hemifield split, inter-looking interval, reciprocation latency, the partner's gaze, fixation counts and durations, pupil size and the trial counts between microstimulation and sham trials, and detects saccades with a port of the Otero-Millan et al. (2014) detector to test their counts and kinematics. The causal decomposition is not run; its cost is timed.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Fan et al. (2024) from dandiset 000959

outcomes.statement: Eyes stimulation was applied on 27 days per stimulated area (OFC, dmPFC and ACCg), 15 per area from monkey L and 12 per area from monkey T, and Mouth stimulation on 5 days per area from monkey T.
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Closed-loop microstimulation protocol, paragraph 1; Figure 1B legend
outcomes.quote: In our main experiments (Eyes stimulation; n = 15 per area from monkey L and n = 12 per area from monkey T)
outcomes.notes: Days holding kept stimulation and sham trials are 15 per area for monkey L, 12 per area for monkey T (Eyes) and 5 per area for monkey T (Mouth). Each day holds one region.

outcomes.statement: Each day held on average 10 live social gaze sessions (9 to 11) and 5 non-social control sessions (4 to 8) for monkey L, and 15 social (14 to 15) and 5 control sessions for monkey T, each 300 s long.
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Experimental setup, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Each data collection day consisted of a total of alternating 10 live social gaze sessions and 5 non-social control sessions on average for monkey L (9-11 social and 4-8 control sessions across all days) and alternating 15 live social gaze sessions and 5 non-social control sessions on average for monkey T (14-15 social and 5 control sessions across all days). Each session lasted 300 sec.
outcomes.notes: Monkey L has 10.0 social runs per day (9 to 11) and 6.02 control runs (4 to 8); monkey T has 14 social runs on every one of its 36 Eyes days and 5 control runs. Runs hold 295.8 to 297.3 s of valid samples (mean 296.4). All ranges hold, and three of four means; monkey L's control mean of 6.02 is outside 5 plus or minus 0.5, as 14 of its 45 days have 8 control runs. Monkey T's mean of 14 is within the tolerance of 15 but no Eyes day has 15 social runs (the Mouth days have 15).
deviations: A session of the paper is taken to be one file (one run); the valid run length is the span of non-NaN samples of `t`.

outcomes.statement: In the live social gaze condition, the total numbers of microstimulations and of shams per day were comparable across the three stimulated areas and between the two monkeys.
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 2; Figure 1E legend
outcomes.quote: The total number of microstimulations (and shams) received per day was comparable across the three stimulated regions and comparable between the two animals both in the social gaze and non-social control conditions (Fig. 1E, live social gaze condition, all p > 0.90

statistics.n: 15 days per area for monkey L and 12 for monkey T

outcomes.notes: Over the 12 rank-sum tests for stimulations and the 12 for shams, the smallest FDR-corrected p is 0.908 and 0.942, so all exceed 0.90 as reported (smallest uncorrected 0.509 and 0.187). Kept trials per day average 116 to 125 per type and area.
deviations: Benjamini-Hochberg correction from statsmodels in place of dsp3.fdr, which the claims file names; both implement the same procedure.

outcomes.statement: In the non-social control condition the numbers of microstimulations and shams per day were also comparable across areas and between monkeys.
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 2; Figure S1D legend
outcomes.quote: Fig. S1D, non-social control condition, all p > 0.10
outcomes.notes: No FDR-corrected p is below 0.05 (smallest 0.108 for stimulations, 0.082 for shams). The paper's "all p > 0.10" does not hold for two sham tests between the monkeys (OFC and dmPFC, corrected 0.082, uncorrected 0.014 and 0.010); monkey T has more control trials per day (71 to 77) than monkey L (52 to 57).

outcomes.statement: The stimulated monkeys made significantly more fixations per day on the partner's Eyes than on the non-eye Face, for days of all three stimulated areas.
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 2; Figure S1E
outcomes.quote: The total number of fixations on partner's Eyes per day was significantly higher than fixations on non-eye Face for all three stimulated brain regions (Fig. S1E, top, all p < 10−4, Wilcoxon signed rank, two-sided, FDR-corrected)
outcomes.notes: Under both day counts (a, total; b, mean per run) and both event sets (M1-only and mutual, M1-only), Eyes fixations exceed non-eye Face fixations for every area, corrected p from 1.1e-07 to 3.1e-05, all below 1e-4. Median day totals are 382 to 408 Eyes and 134 to 179 non-eye Face fixations.
deviations: The events counted are not fixed by the claims file. M1's fixations in the ROI including the M1 side of mutual events are the main set, following the Methods' "total number of gaze fixations ... of the stimulated monkey" (STAR Methods, Frequency of microstimulations and regions of interest); M1-only events are shown and give the same outcome.

The non-eye Face is the files' m1_neface table, which includes the Mouth, with mutual_face and mutual_mouth for mutual events (mutual_face is the face outside the Eyes and the Mouth; the notebook shows that m1_wholeface equals m1_eye plus m1_neface and that mutual_wholeface equals mutual_eye plus mutual_face plus mutual_mouth).

outcomes.statement: The number of fixations on the partner's Eyes per day was comparable to the number of fixations on the RDM stimulus, for days of all three areas.
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 2; Figure S1E
outcomes.quote: the total number of fixations on partner's Eyes per day was comparable to fixations on the RDM stimulus for days involving the three stimulated regions (Fig. S1E, top, all p > 0.30)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), the day's total, which the criterion judges, Eyes fixations exceed RDM fixations for every area (corrected p 0.00036, 0.000025 and 0.00041 for OFC, dmPFC and ACCg; median differences 177, 202 and 241 per day). A day holds about twice as many social runs as control runs (L 10 and 6, T 14 and 5), so day totals differ. Under the code's reading (b), the mean per run, the counts are comparable (corrected p 0.40, 0.40 and 0.52), as the paper reports; M1-only events give the same pattern under both readings. Whether the claims file's deciding reading (a) misreads the paper, given about twice as many social runs as control runs per day, is asked of a reader in questions/000959.yaml; the outcome is judged on the claims file as it stands.
deviations: The RDM fixations are the M1 events labelled Eyes in the Dot runs, whose Eyes ROI is the RDM location ("same location and size as Eyes ROI", STAR Methods, Closed-loop microstimulation protocol).

outcomes.statement: After OFC microstimulations, compared with shams, the stimulated monkey's fixations in the 1.5 s post-gaze epoch were more clustered around the partner monkey.
outcomes.source: Results, Closed-loop microstimulations of OFC facilitate momentary social attention in the spatial dimension, paragraph 2; Figure 2A
outcomes.quote: Specifically, microstimulations of OFC led to more clustered subsequent gaze fixations around the partner monkey (Fig. 2A
outcomes.notes: The day-averaged OFC stimulation minus sham density summed over the whole Face squares is 7.47 (z-scored) and 0.0093 (by total), and over the Eyes squares 3.71 and 0.0046; it is positive in each monkey under each normalisation. dmPFC (whole Face -2.56 and -0.0027) and ACCg (-2.55 and -0.0048) are negative. 10,771 of 53,542 post-gaze fixations fall outside the 40-degree grid.
deviations: Fixations are the Methods reading (M1-only and mutual events). The grid is centred on each run's Eyes ROI centre, and the ROI squares are those whose centres lie in the ROI rectangle, relative to the Eyes centre, of every social run of the day, a standard choice; the three recalibrated days, which have two ROI sets, are dmPFC and ACCg days. Pixels are converted with 27 cm at 50 cm over 768 pixels (claims file, opening comment).

outcomes.statement: OFC microstimulations decreased the social gaze distance, the mean distance of the stimulated monkey's fixations in the post-gaze epoch from the centre of the partner's Eyes, compared with shams; the effect held in each monkey.
outcomes.source: Results, Closed-loop microstimulations of OFC facilitate momentary social attention in the spatial dimension, paragraph 3; Figure 2C legend
outcomes.quote: microstimulations of OFC significantly decreased the average distance of one's own gaze positions in space relative to partner's Eyes during the post-gaze epoch, compared to shams (Fig. 2C, p < 0.001, Wilcoxon signed rank, two-sided
outcomes.notes: Methods reading, median stimulation minus sham day difference -17.9 pixels (-0.70 degrees), p = 0.00021 over 27 days; monkey L p = 0.0067 (paper 0.008), monkey T p = 0.016 (paper 0.002), both negative. Code reading, p = 0.00013, 0.0067 and 0.0034. 1,270 of 19,474 social trials have no fixation in the window and are left out of the day means.
deviations: The mutual events added in the Methods reading are the M1 side of mutual_wholeface, which holds every mutual event (mutual_eye, mutual_face and mutual_mouth are subsets of it, shown in the notebook); mutual events are defined only within the face, and m1_all holds no M1 side of a mutual event.
Each run's own ROIs are used, since three days were recalibrated between runs (08142019, 12102019, 12132019).

outcomes.statement: Microstimulations of dmPFC or ACCg did not change social gaze distance.
outcomes.source: Results, Closed-loop microstimulations of OFC facilitate momentary social attention in the spatial dimension, paragraph 3; Figure 2C
outcomes.quote: By contrast, we did not observe such stimulation effect on social gaze distance for dmPFC (Fig. 2C, p = 0.361) or ACCg (Fig. 2C, p = 0.374)
outcomes.notes: dmPFC median day difference -6.5 pixels, p = 0.21; ACCg -4.9 pixels, p = 0.39 (paper 0.361 and 0.374). The code reading gives 0.29 and 0.29.

outcomes.source: Results, Closed-loop microstimulations of OFC facilitate momentary social attention in the spatial dimension, paragraph 3; Figure 2E

outcomes.source: Results, Closed-loop microstimulations of OFC facilitate momentary social attention in the spatial dimension, paragraph 4; Figure 2G-H
outcomes.quote: The absence of stimulation effect for the RDM stimulus was also found when gaze fixation locations were split by hemifield for OFC (Fig. 2G–H; contralateral: p = 0.097; ipsilateral: p = 0.249; contralateral vs. ipsilateral: p = 0.442), dmPFC (p = 0.374; p = 0.517; p = 0.773) or ACCg (p = 0.532; p = 0.943; p = 0.171)

outcomes.statement: OFC microstimulations decreased the inter-looking interval, the latency of the stimulated monkey to look back at the partner's whole Face within 5 s after the trial, compared with shams; dmPFC and ACCg microstimulations did not.
outcomes.source: Results, Microstimulations of OFC also promote momentary social attention in the temporal dimension, Inter-looking interval, paragraph 1; Figure 3B legend
outcomes.quote: Microstimulations of OFC decreased this inter-looking interval (Fig. 3B, p = 0.035, Wilcoxon signed rank, two-sided; see Fig. S3A for an alternative visualization). However, we did not observe such stimulation effect for dmPFC (Fig. 3B, p = 0.792) or ACCg (Fig. 3B, p = 0.291)
outcomes.notes: OFC median day difference -0.069 s, p = 0.044 (paper 0.035); dmPFC p = 0.77, ACCg 0.34 (paper 0.792, 0.291); monkey L 0.25 and T 0.11 (paper 0.188, 0.092). The outcome is near the threshold and depends on two details. 91 trials have a whole Face event that starts at the trial sample itself; the criterion's "starts after it" leaves them out, and counting them as latency 0 gives OFC p = 0.058. M1-only events give OFC p = 0.0022 (T 0.0024).
deviations: An event "after" the trial must start later than the trial's own sample (criterion, "starts after it"); 91 events that start on the trial sample, likely the triggering fixation as the offline fixation detection saw it, are not counted. Whether the paper's code counts them is not known; this is asked of the paper's authors in the findings.

outcomes.statement: Microstimulations did not change the relative causal strength of gaze between the monkeys in any area.
outcomes.source: Results, Do microstimulations of OFC also lead to longer timescale modulation of social gaze exchanges?, paragraph 1; Figure S4A legend
outcomes.quote: We did not observe stimulation effect on the magnitudes of relative causal strength (OFC ... dmPFC ... ACCg
outcomes.notes: The relative causal strength needs the causal decomposition of Yang, Peng and Huang (2018), whose code runs 2 + 2 x (number of IMFs) ensemble EMDs per trial, each with 10 fixed sifts per IMF. Neither the noise level nor the ensemble size has a default in that code, and its example uses 1,000 ensembles, as does the claims file's reading (a), so both readings cost the same. In the run recorded here, one EEMD of one 150-bin series with 1,000 ensembles takes 15.9 s on one core with PyEMD (6.8 s on four processes; the round-2 run gave 13.1 and 5.5 s, so the timing varies between runs) and yields 7 IMFs, so a trial takes about 255 CPU s, and the 19,474 social Eyes trials about 1,380 CPU hours (about 591 hours of wall time on four processes). A compiled implementation at 10 microseconds per cubic-spline envelope would still need about 104 CPU hours. The notebook limit is one hour. The trials, distances and epochs the analysis would use are all in the dataset.

Reading (b), M1-only events, gives dmPFC 28 ms, p = 0.028 and OFC p = 0.36. The claim holds for OFC and not for dmPFC. ACCg, outside the claim, gives 0.30 and 0.13. 13,779 of 19,474 trials fall inside an offline Eyes event under (a), 12,647 under (b); the 5,695 others under (a) are spread evenly over areas and trial types (27.3% to 30.1%; stimulation minus sham per day, dmPFC p = 0.069, OFC 0.58), 4,227 of them fall inside another M1 fixation (2,036 outside the face, 1,600 on the non-eye face), and 609 have an Eyes event starting within 20 ms after the trial. statistics.test: Wilcoxon signed rank, two-sided, per 10 ms bin

outcomes.notes: No 10-ms bin of the 70 gives p below 0.05 in any area; the smallest p are 0.31 (OFC), 0.51 (dmPFC) and 0.11 (ACCg). 2,198 of 19,474 social trials keep M1's gaze in the whole Face for 700 ms; all 27 days of each area have both trial types.

outcomes.statement: The numbers of microsaccades and macrosaccades in the post-gaze epoch did not differ between microstimulation and sham trials for OFC or dmPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Microstimulation effects of OFC and dmPFC are not driven by low-level properties of saccades, paragraph 1; Figure 5C-D
outcomes.quote: number of microsaccades (Fig. 5C, OFC
outcomes.notes: With the claims file's reading (a), a microsaccade lying strictly within an M1 fixation, microsaccade counts do not change for OFC (p = 0.069; paper 0.456) or dmPFC (0.89; paper 0.581) and macrosaccade counts do not change for dmPFC (0.24; paper 0.230), but OFC stimulation trials have fewer macrosaccades (median day difference -0.069 per post-gaze epoch, p = 0.044; paper 0.055). One of the four tests fails. With the paper's code's labelling, reading (b), none does (smallest 0.15). ACCg, outside the claim, gives p = 0.009 (micro) and 0.004 (macro) under (a). The detector finds 454,642 saccades in the 1,179 social runs (386 per run), median duration 147 ms (95th percentile 1,062 ms), median amplitude 13.7 degrees; in one run the gaze velocity inside fixations has a median of 19.7 deg/s and is under the detector's 5 deg/s saccade limit for 5.4% of samples, so many detected saccades span several fixations. In 202 of the 1,179 runs the MATLAB code's merge of overlapping saccades would not pair starts and ends. The port was not run against the MATLAB code, which is not available here. On synthetic gaze with little noise it finds all 93 saccades with their durations (median 38 ms detected and true); with white noise that gives the data's velocity inside fixations (median 19.8 deg/s, 4.3% under 5 deg/s) it finds 86.7% and doubles their median duration (72.5 against 37.5 ms; 95th percentile 172 ms). The data's durations are longer still, so their noise is not only white. The outcome rests on the assumption stated in the deviations, and the micro/macro labelling changes it (reading b gives 0 of 4).
deviations: Assumption. The detection here is taken to stand in for the paper's. The paper names the software (Key resources table, Otero-Millan et al. 2014) and says it "captured both canonical microsaccades ... and macrosaccades" (STAR Methods, Control analyses), but not whether the gaze was filtered first, and it reports no property of the detected saccades. The paper's code passes M1's gaze unfiltered (script/detect_microsaccades.m at cc0bf994), so unfiltered gaze is the best-supported choice, and the files' gaze is taken to be the gaze the paper passed. On these data the detector's output is not physiological (median duration 147 ms, 95th percentile 1,062 ms, velocity inside fixations under the 5 deg/s limit for 5.4% of samples in one run), which a filter would change; whether the paper's saccades looked the same is asked of the paper's authors in the findings.

The dataset holds no saccade events. Saccades are detected with a Python port of the Otero-Millan et al. (2014) detector, from the authors' MATLAB code at a pinned commit (inputs), with that code's defaults, called as the paper's code calls it (script/run_saccade_detection.m and script/detect_microsaccades.m at cc0bf994; M1's gaze in degrees from the first valid time sample, passed as both eyes, NaN samples as blinks). The claim is with_inputs for that software, as the claims file says.

The port uses scipy's k-means (Lloyd iterations from the same starting centres) in place of MATLAB's kmeans, and merges overlapping saccades as a union in the 202 runs where the MATLAB code would stop with an error.

The fixations that define a microsaccade are the files' M1 fixations (M1-only and mutual), the EyeMMV events the claims file names; the paper's code detects its own fixations (is_fixation with 20, 10 and 0.03), and its labelling, reading (b), counts a saccade as a microsaccade when its start is at least 50 samples after a fixation's start and before its end (script/label_saccades.m).

outcomes.statement: Microstimulations of OFC or dmPFC did not change macrosaccade peak velocity, the slope of peak velocity on amplitude, or that slope by saccade direction.
outcomes.source: Results, Microstimulation effects of OFC and dmPFC are not driven by low-level properties of saccades, paragraph 1; Figure 5E-H
outcomes.quote: macrosaccade peak velocity (Fig. 5E, OFC
outcomes.notes: With reading (a) of the macrosaccade, none of the 14 OFC and dmPFC tests gives p below 0.05. Peak velocity of the first macrosaccade, OFC p = 0.052 and dmPFC 0.88 (paper 0.848, 1); slope difference against zero 0.70 and 0.59 (paper 0.665, 0.904); permutation 0.28 and 0.19 (paper 0.515, 0.164); by direction group the smallest p is 0.071 (OFC CI; paper all above 0.47 and 0.31). With the paper's code's labelling, reading (b), 3 of the 14 give p below 0.05 (dmPFC slope difference 0.030, OFC IC 0.048, dmPFC CC 0.037), so the result depends on how microsaccades are told from macrosaccades. 15,961 of 19,474 trials have a first macrosaccade under (a), 11,354 under (b). The outcome rests on the same assumption as fig5cd-saccade-counts-unchanged, that this detection on the files' unfiltered gaze stands in for the paper's.
deviations: Assumption, as for fig5cd-saccade-counts-unchanged. The detection on the files' unfiltered gaze, as the paper's code passes it, is taken to stand in for the paper's, whose detected saccades are not described; the detector's output on these data is not physiological (median duration 147 ms), and the labelling of micro- and macrosaccades changes the count of failing tests (0 of 14 under reading a, 3 of 14 under b).

Saccades as in fig5cd-saccade-counts-unchanged (a Python port of the Otero-Millan et al. 2014 detector, with_inputs). Slopes are least-squares lines over at least 3 saccades per trial type and day; the permutation seed 5 is a standard choice. Hemifields of the saccade's start and end are taken against the centre of roi_m2_face, as for the fixations.

findings.statement: The dataset holds 6.0 control (Dot) runs per day on average for monkey L (4 to 8; 14 of 45 days have 8), where the paper reports 5 on average, and 14 social runs on every Eyes day of monkey T, where the paper reports 15 on average (14 to 15). Either some runs were not analysed in the paper or the counts in the paper are off; the files do not say which runs the paper used. On the 14 monkey L days with 8 control runs, the runs are numbered 1 to 8, each 295.8 to 296.9 s long with 9 to 32 kept trials, so nothing in the files marks any of them as extra.

The Methods give the fixation counts of Figure S1E as the total per day, and the paper's code takes the mean per session. Because a day has about twice as many social runs as control runs, the Eyes against RDM comparison is significant for every area with day totals (corrected p 0.000025 to 0.00041) and comparable with means per run (0.40 to 0.52), as the paper reports.

Neither the files nor the paper give the padding of the Eyes ROI (the Methods text has the number missing), nor how fixation events were assigned to ROIs. 6% of the M1 Eyes events of social runs and 11% of those of Dot runs have a mean gaze position outside the Eyes rectangle of their file, and 3% and 10% of whole Face events outside the Face rectangle. The description of `laterality_label` does not name its reference; it matches the centre of `roi_m2_face` for 99.98% of M1 events.

The Dot (control) runs do not hold `roi_m2_face`, the reference of their hemifield split, nor say that their `roi_m1_eyes` is the RDM stimulus; both are inferred, the first from the same day's social runs and the second from the Methods.

Question for the paper's authors. For the inter-looking interval, does a whole Face event that starts on the trial sample itself (91 trials; likely the triggering fixation as the offline detection found it) count as the look back with latency 0? Counting it changes the OFC day-level p from 0.044 to 0.058. And is the inter-looking interval taken over M1-only events or M1-only and mutual events, as the Methods say (OFC p 0.0022 against 0.044)?

Question for the paper's authors. Is M2's reciprocation latency measured from the start of M1's look at M2 or from the trial time? Measured from M1's look, dmPFC gives p = 0.044; from the trial, no area is below 0.46. And how is the p-value of the Eyes against Mouth bootstrap computed (one- or two-sided, and which tail)?

Trial times fall inside an offline M1 event in the triggering ROI on 71% of social Eyes trials and 62% of Dot Eyes trials, against 5 to 20% for times shifted by 0.5 to 2 s; this is consistent with a shared clock of trials and events, and shows that about 30% of online triggers do not coincide with an offline fixation in the ROI (65 of 954 social Eyes runs are below 50%).

The fixation tables are named alike but cut the face differently. m1_neface (and m2_neface) is the face outside the Eyes and includes the Mouth (all 23,641 m1_mouth events are in it), while mutual_face is the face outside both the Eyes and the Mouth (mutual_wholeface equals mutual_eye plus mutual_face plus mutual_mouth). The table descriptions do not say so.

The files hold no saccade events. Run on M1's gaze as the paper's code calls it, the Otero-Millan et al. (2014) detector finds 386 saccades per social run with a median duration of 147 ms and a 95th percentile of 1,062 ms; the gaze velocity inside fixations (median about 20 deg/s in one run) is above the detector's 5 deg/s saccade limit for about 95% of samples, so many detected saccades span several fixations. In 202 of 1,179 social runs, the MATLAB code's merge of overlapping saccades yields unequal numbers of starts and ends, where that code would stop with an error. Whether the paper's gaze was filtered before detection is not stated.

Question for the paper's authors. Was M1's gaze filtered before the Otero-Millan et al. (2014) detector was run, and what durations and amplitudes did the detected saccades have? Run on the files' gaze unfiltered, as script/detect_microsaccades.m passes it, the detector gives a median duration of 147 ms (95th percentile 1,062 ms), and the two saccade outcomes (OFC macrosaccade counts p = 0.044 against the paper's 0.055; 0 of 14 kinematics tests failing) rest on this detection standing in for the paper's. With the code's labelling of microsaccades the counts give no failing test and the kinematics 3 of 14.

The verifier tested helper functions on synthetic inputs and checked signrank against a normal approximation. Its report had no attempt record and gave its own outcome for each claim; 35 of 36 agree with the record as it then stood.

disagreements.reason: Cell 68: OFC holds (p = 0.61 / 0.36), but dmPFC triggering fixations are longer after stimulation under both readings (p = 0.019 / 0.028; paper 0.269). 29% of trials (5,695 of 19,474) have no M1 Eyes event in progress at the trial time; this selection is left uninvestigated, and the failing dmPFC test depends on it (B6).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agrees with 34 of the 36 outcomes; for the two saccade claims it agrees with the outcomes as computed but asks that they be marked as resting on an assumption. It also corrected the headline counts of its round-1 report (22 reproduced, 4 partially reproduced, 2 not reproduced and 8 blocked), and reported that the Summary's "6% of the M1 Eyes events have a mean position outside the Eyes rectangle" holds only for social runs (6.3%; Dot runs 10.7%); the Summary now gives both.

disagreements.reason: Agrees with the outcome as computed, but it rests on an assumption that is not stated. The detector's output is not physiological: cell 101 gives a median saccade duration of 147 ms, 95th percentile 1,062 ms, median amplitude 13.7 degrees and 386 saccades per run, and in cell 102 gaze velocity inside fixations has a median of 19.7 deg/s and is under the 5 deg/s limit for only 5.4% of samples. The micro/macro labels may not mean much, as the record says many detected saccades span several fixations. The outcome depends on the labelling (reading b gives 0 of 4 failing tests, against 1 of 4 under a), and the port was never checked against the MATLAB code on any sample. The outcome depends on this detection standing in fairly for the paper's, including that the paper did not filter the gaze first, and should be marked assumed: true with the assumption stated; it is not clearly reasonable given the notebook's own diagnostics.

entries.name: 000959-fan-2024
entries.title: Closed-loop OFC microstimulation and dynamic social attention (Fan et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Fan, Dal Monte, Nair, Fagan and Chang (2024) on dandiset 000959, which holds the gaze, pupil, fixation events and stimulation times of every run of the 81 Eyes and 15 Mouth stimulation days of two stimulated monkeys. It compares social gaze distance, its hemifield split, inter-looking interval, reciprocation latency, the partner's gaze, fixation counts and durations, pupil size and the trial counts between microstimulation and sham trials, and detects saccades with a port of the Otero-Millan et al. (2014) detector to test their counts and kinematics. The causal decomposition is not run; its cost is timed.
